name: Expose a custom post type to core/read-content and use AI plugin 1.3.0 features
query: Our site runs the canonical WordPress AI plugin 1.3.0 and our own plugin registers a 'recipe' custom post type. Three asks: (1) make recipes readable by AI agents through the AI plugin's read abilities, (2) let comment moderators generate reply suggestions, and (3) raise the request timeout for image generation to 60 seconds. What's the right integration?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router / wp-project-triage to classify the repo as a downstream plugin extending the AI plugin; route to wp-ai-plugin (wp-abilities-api as secondary reference)

Step 2: For (1), establish first that core/read-content only registers when the Custom Abilities experiment is enabled — 1.3.0 moved the five built-in read abilities behind that opt-in gate, so on a fresh 1.3.0 site the ability does not exist at all; enabling it needs both the global wpai_features_enabled switch and wpai_feature_custom-abilities_enabled
Step 3: Recognize that once the gate is on, core/read-content only surfaces post types flagged with show_in_abilities — the fix is registration-side, not a new REST controller or a custom ability

Step 4: Add 'show_in_abilities' => true to the register_post_type( 'recipe', ... ) args, and ensure registration runs before the Abilities API initializes (wp_abilities_api_init) so the post type lands in the ability's input schema

Step 5: Know that WordPress core does not ship the show_in_abilities flag natively yet — the AI plugin polyfills it onto curated core objects in includes/Abilities/Show_In_Abilities.php, run once by the Custom Abilities experiment; custom post types opt in via their own registration args
Step 6: Resolve the ability defensively with wp_get_ability() and handle null rather than assuming the ID exists

Step 7: For (2), do NOT build a custom experiment — Suggest Reply ships since 1.2.0 (Experiment 'suggest-reply', ability 'ai/suggest-reply', Experiment_Category::ADMIN); enable it on Settings → AI (per-feature toggles; configuration lives under the collapsed 'Advanced settings' section since 1.2.0)
Step 8: For (3), filter wpai_default_request_timeout — signature ( int $default_timeout, string $feature_id ) — returning 60 for the image-generation feature id

Step 9: Know that wp_ai_client_default_request_timeout is a different, real filter: it is WordPress core's, applied in WP_AI_Client_Prompt_Builder at builder construction and receiving only the timeout. The plugin's changelog mislabels its own filter with that name; pick by scope
Step 10: Gate all downstream code on function_exists( 'wp_supports_ai' ) && wp_supports_ai() and class_exists checks so nothing fatals when the AI plugin is deactivated

Step 11: Verify: with Custom Abilities enabled, /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities lists core/read-content, executing it with post_type=recipe returns readable recipes (raw fields only for posts the user can edit), and the Suggest reply row action appears on the Comments screen
success_criteria: States that core/read-content is gated behind the Custom Abilities experiment as of AI plugin 1.3.0 and does not present it as always registered
Solves the exposure ask with 'show_in_abilities' => true on register_post_type — NOT by writing a new ability, REST controller, or setting show_in_rest alone
States the timing constraint: the post type must be registered with the flag before wp_abilities_api_init / abilities registration snapshots it
References Show_In_Abilities.php as the polyfill and notes core will own the flag later (like show_in_rest)
Resolves abilities with wp_get_ability() and handles absence instead of assuming the ID
Reuses the built-in Suggest Reply experiment (ai/suggest-reply) instead of building a duplicate
Uses the real filter name wpai_default_request_timeout with the ( $default_timeout, $feature_id ) signature
Describes wp_ai_client_default_request_timeout accurately as core's own filter rather than a name that does not exist
Includes the wp_supports_ai() / class_exists guards for downstream code
Verification step exercises /wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities and notes permission-gated field access (raw fields require edit capability)
